rows.label: expert
rows.name: Thermal noise floor and CNR
rows.formula: Ln = 10·log10(k·T·B·R / 10^−6); single CNR = I − NF − Ln; N equal CNR = single − 10·log10(N); combined = −10·log10(sum(10^(−CNRi/10)))
rows.source: Expert matched-load thermal model. k is the SI Boltzmann constant. T is the 290 K noise-figure reference. R is 75 ohms, an expert cable-model assumption. The written check cites the BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, section 2.2, SCTE 270 2021r1 sections 12–14 and 15.5, and SCTE 293-11 2025 sections 5.2–5.5. Those PDFs were not opened for this row
rows.locator: handoff_docs/reviews/chatgpt-roadmap-critique.md, cascade section and cases C1–C4; night-sweep/field-calcs.js cascade. Checked against handoff_docs/reviews/chatgpt-calculator-test-vectors.json
rows.conditions: Equivalent noise bandwidth B in hertz, entered by the user. Fixed 290 K and a matched 75 ohm load; temperature is not editable and a mismatched source and load is refused. Single-amplifier CNR uses the carrier input and a noise figure that applies to that frequency and configuration. NF below 0 is outside this narrowed model, not a claim that a negative noise figure is impossible. N is a count of equal independent receiver-referred noise contributions, not a count of identical model names. Combined CNR is an uncorrelated power combination of CNR values already referred to the same carrier, plane and bandwidth. Optical CNR is optional and is left out when it is not entered. No CTB/CSO score, no MER prediction, no ordered Friis chain and no return-leg shortcut from a stage count alone. No company target. 42/54 and 204/258 are not inputs. The six-significant-figure display is a presentation choice, not an RF tolerance.
